findings.title: Current State Law Governing Certain Protections for Personal Identifiable Information Did Not Apply to State Agencies
findings.description: Current state law protecting personal identifiable information (PII) does not apply to State agencies, and the DoIT Policy did not address notification requirements established in State law for businesses. The audit found that while State law mandates protections for businesses, no similar statewide policy existed for State agencies.
findings.recommendation: DoIT should propose legislation to address the protection of PII in the custody of State government agencies and develop a security breach notification policy until such legislation is enacted.

findings.title: DoIT Did Not Have a Formal Process in Place to Enforce the Provisions of its Information Security Policy
findings.description: DoIT had not developed a formal mechanism designed to monitor and enforce the provisions of its Policy, delegating responsibility to individual agencies due to lack of resources. Consequently, there was a lack of assurance that State agencies were complying with the provisions of the Policy.
findings.recommendation: DoIT should implement a process to monitor and enforce agency compliance with the Policy, such as requiring the use of an agency self-assessment tool.

findings.title: DoIT Could Improve Guidance to Help Agencies Address Certain Security Issues
findings.description: DoIT's Policy referred to NIST standards but often did not provide additional information or guidance for implementation, such as specific instructions for incident handling or security monitoring methods.
findings.recommendation: DoIT should review the comprehensiveness of its existing Policy guidance and provide additional instruction or guidance as necessary to agencies for implementing components of agency security programs.

findings.title: DoIT Needs to Develop a More Responsive Process to Address Emerging Technologies and a Policy Regarding Mobile Devices
findings.description: DoIT did not always promptly address significant changes in technology impacting information security, such as cloud computing services used by agencies for years without policy guidance. Additionally, DoIT had not developed comprehensive policies designed to guide agencies regarding mobile device security.
findings.recommendation: DoIT should develop a process to more timely address the security implications of emerging technologies and issue a comprehensive statewide policy regarding minimum security requirements for mobile devices.

findings.title: DoIT Had Not Developed Recommended Practices for Implementing Data Loss Prevention Solutions
findings.description: DoIT had not developed recommended practices for State agencies to address data loss prevention (DLP) solutions, which detect and prevent unauthorized transmission of confidential information.
findings.recommendation: DoIT should develop policy and guidance regarding the implementation of a data loss prevention strategy and assist State agencies in researching, obtaining, and implementing data loss prevention tools.

findings.title: State Agencies Often Did Not Document the Security Categorization of Information Systems
findings.description: Only one of the five agencies reviewed had assigned security levels to all information systems; others did not assign categories or only for certain systems. Determining security category is integral for assessing risks associated with data confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
findings.recommendation: State agencies should comply with DoIT Policy by evaluating and documenting security categories for all of their information systems and establish security measures commensurate with data sensitivity and risk.

findings.title: Certain Agencies' Information Security Policies Were Not Agency Specific or Did Not Include All Required Components
findings.description: One agency's security policy did not address security certification and accreditation, while another copied DoIT language without guidance on implementation. Three agencies met the criteria by developing adequate agency-specific information security policies.
findings.recommendation: State agencies should develop an agency-specific information security policy that addresses the required components of an overall information security program established by the DoIT Policy.

findings.title: Risk Management Processes Were Not Fully Implemented
findings.description: None of the five state agencies selected for review had fully implemented a risk management process; none consistently completed risk assessments for all information systems. Agency policies generally did not specify how often or under what circumstances to complete or update risk assessments.
findings.recommendation: State agencies should develop and document a risk management process including risk assessments that apply to all critical systems, specify frequency of re-evaluation, perform assessments for all critical systems currently in use, and periodically update or re-evaluate the risk assessments.

findings.title: Security Awareness Training Was Not Always Provided to Employees or Tracked
findings.description: Three agencies did not adequately ensure or document that employees received required training. For example, one agency tracked locations visited but not actual employee attendance, and another found new employees often did not attend training within the required 60 days.
findings.recommendation: Agencies should provide timely security awareness training to all employees and document employee attendance at the training.

findings.title: Data Contained on Portable Devices Was Not Always Properly Protected
findings.description: Two of the five agencies tested did not implement practices such as full disk encryption to ensure confidential information on agency-issued devices was protected. The other three agencies implemented procedures to encrypt such information.
findings.recommendation: State agencies should ensure that all confidential information contained on portable devices is encrypted as required by DoIT Policy and develop a process to periodically verify that all portable devices hosting confidential information are properly protected.

findings.title: State Agencies Were in Various Stages of Implementing Data Loss Prevention Tools and Techniques
findings.description: Two agencies had implemented data loss prevention tools to monitor e-mail activity for patterns resembling social security numbers. The remaining three agencies reviewed had not investigated or implemented the use of DLP tools.
findings.recommendation: State agencies should determine if implementation of DLP tools is appropriate and feasible based on agency data and resources, and if appropriate, implement DLP tools and take appropriate action based on the related results.

findings.title: State Agencies Had Varied Practices in Implementing Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing
findings.description: Three agencies routinely performed vulnerability scanning for their information systems, but two had not implemented any such practice. Two of the three performing scans also performed penetration testing on certain systems.
findings.recommendation: State agencies should develop and implement a vulnerability scanning process on a routine basis, follow up on results to remediate vulnerabilities, determine the feasibility of penetration testing, and perform it when indicated.

extraction.agency_response_summary: DoIT agreed with most recommendations but opposed Recommendation 2 regarding enforcement resources due to staffing constraints; selected state agencies generally agreed with findings and provided completion dates for corrective actions.
extraction.extraction_notes: Audit period derived from fieldwork dates (May 2011 to December 2011). Report date derived from header (September 2012). No dollar amounts explicitly tied to findings were found. Finding 12 had no agency response included in the text.
